findings.reason: implemented as written, a detector meant to be stat-only silently reintroduces a git subprocess on the login node over GPFS; a separate index-committed identity helper (or carrying `.git/index` only in the detector's own signal) satisfies the mechanism without breaking `_head_identity`'s "changes exactly when the commit changes" contract.
findings.text: §2 extends `_head_identity` (serve.py:1291) "to include the stat identity of `.git/index`"; `_head_identity`'s only caller is `_git_head` (serve.py:1319), which memoises the resolved sha on that identity tuple and whose docstring promises an unchanged checkout "start[s] no git process". Adding `.git/index` makes the identity change on every add/merge/pull even when HEAD does not, so the memo (serve.py:1341) misses and spawns a `git rev-parse HEAD` subprocess per index write, and line 59's own done-when asserts precisely this new behaviour ("`_head_identity` changes when `.git/index` changes and HEAD does not") without noting the cost it introduces.

findings.reason: the plan cites the correct owner by name and its done-when edits a file that becomes the newest mtime, so the node builds the mechanism the plan intends; only the prose overstates what the object computes.
findings.text: §2 calls the slow signal "the stat signature of every covered file", but its cited owner `_walk_discovery_signature` reduces the swept files to `(file count, newest mtime)` (documented at serve.py:1631, and it returns that pair at serve.py:1691), so it senses an in-place edit only when the edited file becomes the newest mtime or the file count changes; an uncommitted edit to a covered file that does not become the newest is invisible to it.
